# dash0_custom_skill (Resource)

Manages a Dash0 Agent0 custom skill. A custom skill is a set of files, led by a `SKILL.md`, that Agent0 can load to follow your organization's instructions. Custom skills are organization-level resources and are not scoped to a dataset.

Skills managed by Terraform accept no `custom_skill:write` grant: members can read them, and optionally delete them, but only the Terraform configuration changes their content.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A custom skill with a SKILL.md and a reference file.
# The skill's name comes from the `name` field of the SKILL.md frontmatter.
resource "dash0_custom_skill" "incident_response" {
  custom_skill_yaml = <<-YAML
kind: Dash0Skill
spec:
  files:
    - relativePath: SKILL.md
      content: |
        ---
        name: incident-response
        description: Triage an incident with the SRE team's runbook.
        ---
        When asked to triage an incident, follow references/runbook.md step by step.
    - relativePath: references/runbook.md
      content: |
        1. Check the error rate of the affected service.
        2. Check the deployments of the last hour.
        3. Post a summary in the incident channel.
YAML
}

# A custom skill shared with a team, which may also delete it.
# spec.permissions replaces the stored grants exactly; omit it to keep the server defaults.
# Grants on a Terraform-managed skill accept custom_skill:read and custom_skill:delete,
# never custom_skill:write.
resource "dash0_custom_skill" "release_notes" {
  custom_skill_yaml = <<-YAML
kind: Dash0Skill
spec:
  files:
    - relativePath: SKILL.md
      content: |
        ---
        name: release-notes
        description: Write release notes in the house style.
        ---
        Write release notes as a bulleted list, one bullet per user-facing change.
  permissions:
    - role: basic_member
      actions: [custom_skill:read]
    - teamId: "<YOUR_TEAM_ID>"
      actions: [custom_skill:read, custom_skill:delete]
YAML
}

# You can also build the YAML from a directory of skill files kept next to the configuration:
#
# resource "dash0_custom_skill" "from_directory" {
#   custom_skill_yaml = yamlencode({
#     kind = "Dash0Skill"
#     spec = {
#       files = [
#         for f in fileset("${path.module}/skills/incident-response", "**") : {
#           relativePath = f
#           content      = file("${path.module}/skills/incident-response/${f}")
#         }
#       ]
#     }
#   })
# }
```

## Schema

### Required

- `custom_skill_yaml` (String) The custom skill definition in YAML format. The YAML must include `kind: Dash0Skill` and `spec.files`, a list of `relativePath` and `content` pairs that must include a `SKILL.md`. The skill's name is read from the `name` field of the `SKILL.md` frontmatter; `metadata.name` is derived by the server and ignored. The optional `spec.permissions` list grants `custom_skill:read` and `custom_skill:delete` to a `role` (`admin` or `basic_member`), a `teamId` or a `userId`, and replaces the stored grants exactly. When `spec.permissions` is omitted, the grants are left as they are, and a new skill gets the server defaults. An `admin` entry sets only `defaultEnabled`; the server always adds an `admin` grant, which drift detection ignores unless you declare one. `custom_skill:write` is rejected on skills Terraform creates, and `spec.source` and `dash0.com/enabled` are always rejected. To ship a skill that is off by default, set `defaultEnabled: false` on its grants; this is supported only in organizations where custom skills belong to their author.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The server-assigned identifier of the custom skill.
- `origin` (String) A unique identifier for the custom skill, automatically generated on creation. Used to reference the custom skill for updates, reads, deletes, and imports. Null for a skill created in the Dash0 UI and adopted with `terraform import`; such a skill is addressed by its `id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/bin/bash
# A skill created by Terraform or the Dash0 CLI is imported by its origin;
# a skill created in the Dash0 UI has no origin and is imported by its id.
terraform import dash0_custom_skill.name "{{ id_or_origin }}"
```
